title: Make /api/voice/tts speak with my MOSS voice on the Contabo server, then give the bare IP trusted HTTPS
why: My server ran MOSS on 127.0.0.1:8789 while the route my page calls only knew ElevenLabs and Piper, so I answered 503 and spoke with the browser's voice. Production runs a commit GitHub does not have, so the fix goes in as a patch applied in place, never by moving HEAD. And a browser only lends me a microphone on HTTPS, so voice needs the certificate too. Let's Encrypt issues 6-day certificates for a bare IP, so no domain is needed.

steps.title: Request a read-only recon: commit deploy/contabo/voice-https-request.json with {"action":"recon"} (or dispatch 'Contabo voice and HTTPS')
steps.why: An owner approves the run in the contabo-production environment. Read the PASS/FAIL lines: commit, drift, services, VOXCPM_BASE_URL, MOSS READY, voice/status and the TTS code. The full report, with the DETAIL lines that map the host, stays in /root/lelu-mission/reports/ on the server.

steps.title: Request action "apply"
steps.why: Backs up (verified), applies deploy/contabo/patches/voice-tts-moss.patch, fails only on type errors the patch introduces, restarts lelu only, and requires a 200 WAV and a 200 48 kHz stream from /api/voice/tts. Otherwise it rolls itself back. dist/ is never touched.

steps.title: Request action "accept"
steps.why: Health, login, Groq and OpenRouter through the brokers, MOSS direct, app TTS (WAV and stream), Whisper transcribing my own synthesized WAV, no credential patterns in dist/, services active. Latency is printed per step.

steps.title: Request https-check, then https-stage, https-issue, https-enable, one at a time
steps.why: stage serves ACME challenges on :80 and runs a Let's Encrypt dry run; issue gets the real 6-day certificate and proves renewal with a dry run; enable adds :443 to the existing app block and reverts itself unless a real TLS connection verifies. HTTP stays up.

steps.title: A person checks microphone and playback on a desktop browser and an iPhone at https://157.173.116.95
steps.why: Hardware cannot be proven from a server: permission prompt, capture, hearing my voice, interrupting me.

steps.title: To undo: action "rollback" (voice) or "https-rollback" / "https-rollback-all"
steps.why: Voice rollback reverses the patch and checks the working tree is byte-identical to before. HTTPS rollback restores the nginx file and removes the firewall rule it added. Rollback material is never deleted.
